e: Borrowed from Latin obnūbilātus, perfect passive participle of obnūbilō (“to cover with clouds or fog”) (see -ate (adjective-forming suffix) and -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from ob- + nūbilō (“be cloudy”), from nūbēs (“cloud”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)newdʰ- (“to cover”). By surface analysis, ob- + Latin nubil- + -ate.
q:
[B]ot sen I the to hir cure vassaill:
 [To mak the r]efrane, my power laikis haill.
 [For] in hir net thow art obnubilate:
 [Gif] thow conuert, and tak my trew counsall
 […]eng or lust thow suld neuer assaill.
 […]waill hart fra hir to sequestrate,
 […] time sa far as is fustrate:

e: Coined by Scientology founder L. Ron Hubbard, apparently as a blend of observe + gnosis.
q: Hubbard created Scientology's language to be unique to its members. It includes words that are interpretations, or variations, of standard terms: "isness," for example, which Scientology's glossaries say, in essence, means "reality." But there are also words that are wholly made up, such as "obnosis," which means "observation of the obvious."
